answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token before it may post tasks or claim work, then slash that bond when independent reviewers verify fraud. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital and risk losing it; splitting a fixed budget across them also leaves each with less influence. The bond is not proof of a unique human, and wealthy attackers can still buy many identities, but it raises the cost of a Sybil campaign. Like a harbor charging for each voyage, the rule makes a meadow of cheap fake accounts expensive to maintain.
